statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds elevated on a 5.18% 10-year Treasury yield and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff that the weekend left in diplomatic deadlock rather than kinetic escalation.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen into the early Asian hours, where the weekend's unpriced content would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail low with futures closed; Stress elevated on a post-GFC-high 10-year while the Hormuz standoff stays diplomatic rather than kinetic
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high, with the Dow up 0.93%, the S&P 500 up 0.51% and VIX down 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

The Stress backdrop remains demanding on two fronts. Rates are the first: H.15 constant maturities put the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year at its highest level since the global financial crisis, and equities absorbed that move on Friday without a volatility bid. The second is the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff. Saturday's rejection of Iran's seven-day reopening plan left the diplomatic track deadlocked, and the Sunday hours have added economic rather than kinetic pressure: the Iranian foreign minister states that Tehran awaits a formal US answer through mediators and that only a negotiated solution resolves the deadlock, the US aviation-sanctions programme continues to ground Iranian carriers, Iraq is seeking humanitarian exemptions and Saudi Arabia has taken the maritime-freedom case to the UN. No new strike or shipping attack has been reported today, and crude prices fell across last week, with WTI at $92.41 and Brent at $104.32. Falling energy prices are not escalation pricing, which is the main reason Stress is held at 63 rather than extended further.

Shared latest-session context is stale beyond its 90-minute freshness bound and only partially collected, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is treated as delayed colour only. What it does show is mixed rather than uniformly aligned: megacaps 6 of 8 higher with roughly 1.9% dispersion and semiconductors 6 of 7 higher, alongside a 0.85% technology sector gain against a 0.58% decline in communication services. Mixed breadth of that kind lowers directional conviction; it does not mechanically raise Tail.

The one genuine forward amplifier is mechanical rather than observed. The CME equity index futures reopen at 22:00Z is where the weekend's unpriced diplomatic content meets thin Sunday-evening liquidity, and a narrow danger window is published from there into 02:00Z. Beyond it the week is dense but well defined: JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, Core PCE with final Q2 GDP on Wednesday at 12:30Z, Micron's fiscal Q4 report after Wednesday's close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday at 12:30Z. Federal funding is not a factor: the continuing resolution signed on 2 September runs to 11 December, so no release is at risk of a data blackout. Every one of those items is a checkpoint, not an automatic block, and none of them is scored as observed structure here.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 range, Stress rose from 46 to 63 and Confidence decayed from 82 to 69 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, oil and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout, and the dominant mode stayed normal because no slot in the window contained observable one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk is held near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday and eases slightly as the session passes without new kinetic escalation, then lifts into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen where the weekend's unpriced diplomatic content meets thin liquidity, peaking at 13 in the following hour. It then decays through the Asian hours on the base assumption that reopen pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery. Confidence falls to a trough just before the reopen while the evidence set ages without refreshing observation, then recovers once a live NQ price path exists again. Every value after the current clock-hour is conditional: no post-reopen gap, continuation, failed retracement or extension has been observed, and any such structure would supersede this published path.
